subs.text: Book two.
Telemachus Sets Sail.
Scene one.
Telemachus Calls the Assembly.
Heralds, sound the call.
Summon the long-haired Achaeans to assembly at first light, every man of them.
He enters with two hounds and takes the seat that belonged to his father.
Who has called us here?
Not once since great Odysseus sailed in the hollow ships have we met in council.
What man had such need, young or old?
Has he word of the army coming home?
Whoever he is, blessings on him for it.
Old sir, that man is not far to seek:
I called you, and the trouble is mine.
I have lost my noble father, who was king among you here and gentle as a father;
and now a greater ruin besides, suitors who beset my mother against her will and devour my house day after day.
By Olympian Zeus and by Themis who seats the councils of men, I call it wrong, and I cannot fight it alone.

scenes.title: The Secret of Penelope's Loom
scenes.card: Antinous blames Penelope, who stalled the suitors for years by weaving a burial cloth by day and secretly unpicking it at night.

subs.text: Scene two.
The Secret of Penelope's Loom.
Bold-tongued Telemachus, do not lay your blame at our door.
It is not the suitors who are at fault but your own mother, that queen of cunning;
three years now, and nearly four, she has cheated the hearts of the Achaeans.
She set up her great loom in the hall, a shroud, she told us, for the lord Laertes,
so no woman of the land could reproach her if he lay in death without a winding-sheet.
All day she wove at that web, and every night, with torches set beside her, she unraveled it thread by thread.
A maid betrayed the trick.
We caught her at the loom and forced the web to its end.
Send her back to her father Icarius, and let her marry the man he names, and the man she chooses.

scenes.title: The Eagles Tear the Air
scenes.card: Two eagles fight above the crowd; an old seer says Odysseus is coming home to punish the suitors, and Eurymachus mocks him.

subs.text: Scene three.
The Eagles Tear the Air.
Antinous, I will never drive from this house the mother who bore me and raised me,
not while my father lives or lies dead far away.
Leave my halls;
feast somewhere else, eat your own stores house to house.
Or stay and devour on, and I will cry to the gods who live forever that a day of reckoning come,
and you die in this house unavenged.
Two eagles descend, wheel over the assembly, and tear at one another before vanishing inland.
Men of Ithaca, hear me.
Odysseus is not long from his people now;
he is near, already sowing death and doom for these men.
I read the birds for him the day he sailed, twenty years from home, all his companions lost,
himself unknown at his return, and it is coming to pass.
Let us stop the suitors now, before the ruin falls on more than them.
Old man, go home and prophesy to your children.
Birds are forever crossing the sunlight, and not all of them mean anything.
Odysseus is dead far away, and a pity you did not die with him.
Keep pouring out omens and goading this angry boy, and your prophecy will cost you a fine you will weep to pay.

scenes.title: Mentor Rebukes Ithaca
scenes.card: Telemachus announces a voyage for news; Mentor scolds the people for doing nothing, but the suitors break up the meeting.

subs.text: Scene four.
Mentor Rebukes Ithaca.
Enough of this.
Give me a swift ship and twenty companions,
for I go to Pylos and to Sparta seeking news of my father so long away.
If I hear he lives and is coming home, I can hold out one year more;
if I hear he is dead, I will raise his mound, pay him all the honors owed, and give my mother to a husband.
Hear me now, men of Ithaca.
Let no sceptered king ever again be kind and gentle, since none of you remembers godlike Odysseus,
who ruled you mild as a father.
I do not begrudge the proud suitors their violence, they wager their own heads on it.
It is you I blame, the many, who sit here dumb and never say one word to shame a few.
Mentor, you crazed old rabble-baiter, would you rouse the town against us?
Fighting men over a dinner is grim work.
Why,
if Ithacan Odysseus himself came home and found us feasting in his hall and set his heart on driving us out,
his wife would have small joy of the husband she longs for;
he would meet an ugly death then and there, one man against so many.
Break it up.
Go back to your fields, all of you.
Citizens disperse and the suitors return to the palace.

scenes.title: Athena Answers on the Shore
scenes.card: Alone on the beach, Telemachus prays; Athena appears in Mentor's shape and promises to find him a ship and crew.

subs.text: Scene five.
Athena Answers on the Shore.
Hear me, god who came yesterday to our house and bade me sail the misty sea for news of my father's return.
All of it the Achaeans thwart, and the suitors first, in their evil insolence.
Hear me now.
Telemachus, you will prove no coward and no fool hereafter,
if one drop of your father's fine spirit is truly in you.
That man made word and deed agree, and so will you;
this voyage will not fail.
I sailed with your father of old, and I will sail with you, and find you a swift ship besides.
Go home now, and move among the suitors as if nothing has changed.
Make ready the stores, wine in two-handled jars and barley meal in tight skins, the marrow of men.
I will gather a willing crew through the town and choose the best ship in sea-girt Ithaca,
and we launch her on the dark water tonight.
The voyage becomes a hidden operation running beneath the suitors' gaze.

scenes.title: The Secret Stores
scenes.card: Telemachus secretly orders supplies from the storeroom, and his old nurse Eurycleia, frightened, swears not to tell his mother.

subs.text: Scene six.
The Secret Stores.
Antinous, take your hand from mine.
Am I to feast in quiet among you who strip my house bare?
I am done with that.
I will make my voyage to Pylos, as a passenger on another man's deck if I must,
and I will bring ruin home to you if the gods grant it.
Telemachus enters the locked storeroom filled with metal, cloth, oil, wine, and meal.
Nurse, draw me twelve jars of wine, the finest after what you keep for that unlucky man,
should Odysseus ever come.
And pour twenty measures of milled barley into stitched skins.
Have it gathered by nightfall, and no one is to know, least of all my mother until I am gone.
Ah, child, why has this thought come into your heart?
You are an only son, beloved, and the sea will eat you as it ate him;
stay and keep what is yours.
But since you will go, I swear it by the gods:
your mother hears nothing from me till the twelfth day, unless she misses you and asks herself.

scenes.title: The Night Launch
scenes.card: Athena gathers a crew, puts the suitors to sleep, and sails with Telemachus through the night.

subs.text: Scene seven.
The Night Launch.
Athena, disguised as Telemachus, recruits crewmen and borrows Noemon's ship.
Telemachus, come out.
Your companions sit at the oars already, waiting on your word;
let us not delay the voyage.
The crew carries provisions from the palace and stows them below deck.
Telemachus boards.
Athena takes the pilot's seat and sends a strong west wind.
The sail fills, libations are poured, and the ship travels through the night.

scenes.world: A dark harbour at night, black water and a moored sailing ship, a single fire on shore, wind rising; day-for-night silent-era seascape.

prologue: At dawn Telemachus calls the people of Ithaca together for the first time in twenty years and demands that the suitors leave his house. The suitors refuse and blame his mother. With Athena's help, he prepares to slip away by ship to find news of his father.
